findings.evidence: `grep -n 'IsReal' Kinematics/Basic.lean` → line 92 `def IsReal (k : PhotonKinematics) : Prop := k.virtuality = 0`. `grep -rn '(Collinear|RealPhoton|MasslessTarget)' EpsilonEridani/` returns only the section headers and docstrings of this file — no declaration by those names exists.
findings.fix: Name the hypotheses, as this PR's own `MinkowskiProductExtensions.lean` does with `minkowskiProduct_self_eq_zero_of_timeComponent_eq_of_spatialPart_eq_smul` and `…_of_spatialPart_eq_smul`; or introduce actual `Prop`-valued predicates (e.g. an `IsCollinearWith`/null-four-momentum predicate) and take them as hypotheses so `_of_realPhoton` names something that exists.
findings.issue: `_of_realPhoton` names no hypothesis and clashes with a real predicate: `PhotonKinematics.IsReal (k) : Prop := k.virtuality = 0` is defined in the same `…Photoproduction.Kinematics` namespace (`Kinematics/Basic.lean:92`) and imported here (line 8), so `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_realPhoton` reads as taking `γ.IsReal`. The actual hypotheses are `q.timeComponent = k` and `q.spatialPart = k • n` — i.e. null *and* collinear, a condition strictly stronger than `IsReal`, with the collinearity the name silently drops (the sibling family marks it `_of_collinearPhoton`). Same at lines 191, 201, 211, 273, 282, 292, 301.

findings.evidence: naming-conventions.md: "it is necessary to describe some of the hypotheses. The word \"of\" is used to separate these hypotheses"; the hypotheses here are `hn : ‖n‖ = 1`, `hq : q.timeComponent = k`, `hq' : q.spatialPart = a • n`, `hP`, `hP'` (lines 112–113, 173–174, 267–268).
findings.fix: Either define the predicates these suffixes claim, or rename after the hypotheses (`_of_timeComponent_eq_of_spatialPart_eq_smul`, `_of_spatialPart_eq_neg_smul`, …) in line with the `Lorentz.Vector` lemmas this file calls.
findings.issue: Same defect in the other role-suffixes: `_of_target` (line 100), `_of_collinearPhoton` (119, 128, 140, 152, 163, 238, 251) and `_of_masslessTarget` (273, 282, 292, 302) describe the physical role of the data, not the hypotheses, contrary to the naming convention's rule that `of` separates the described hypotheses. The repo's own precedent is `_of_<existing predicate>` (`eq_of_eqOn_euclideanSection_of_spaceLike`, `trace_total_of_diracEq`, `_of_isHermitian`), where the suffix names a declaration.

findings.evidence: Rapidity.lean:62 definition and lines 18–20 of the module docstring: "This is the physical rapidity along `n` only for a unit vector". No `rapidity` declaration exists upstream to constrain the convention (`grep -ri rapidity upstream/Physlib upstream/mathlib` finds only prose and `γ_tanh`).
findings.fix: Normalise in the definition — `artanh (⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫ / (‖n‖ * v.timeComponent))` — which makes the name correct for any non-zero direction and turns `rapidity_smul_right` into a genuine invariance lemma; or take a bundled unit vector (`Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) 1`).
findings.issue: `rapidity v n = artanh (⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫ / v⁰)` is named for a quantity it computes only when `‖n‖ = 1`; the file itself proves the name is wrong otherwise (`rapidity_smul_right_eq_artanh`, line 72). A user writing `v.rapidity p.spatialPart` gets a term named "rapidity" that is not one, and every consumer lemma must re-carry `‖n‖ = 1`.

summary: The `_of_<role>` suffixes throughout `InvariantMass.lean` name section headers rather than hypotheses, and `_of_realPhoton` in particular collides with the existing `PhotonKinematics.IsReal` predicate in the same namespace, which is not the hypothesis. `Lorentz.Vector.rapidity` also carries a name that is correct only under the unguarded side condition `‖n‖ = 1`.
